newsitem.title: USA: Bad weather delays U.S. weather satellite.
newsitem.headline: Bad weather delays U.S. weather satellite.

text.p: NASA postponed the launch of a much-needed $220 million weather satellite on Wednesday because of stormy weather at the launch site.

The launch of the Atlas rocket carrying the GOES-K weather satellite had been scheduled for early on Thursday but was delayed 24 hours because of storms and gusty winds in the Cape Canaveral area, NASA spokesman George Diller said.
The satellite's blastoff was rescheduled for 1:49 a.m. EDT (0549 GMT) on Friday, when weather conditions were forecast to be near-perfect.

GOES-K is to serve as a much-needed spare for two older satellites already stationed in orbit 22,300 miles (35,890 km) above the equator. Those satellites have suffered technical problems and forecasters are eager to have a back-up in place should one of them fail.

Meteorologists across North America rely on the twin satellites to warn of thunderstorms, flash floods and other severe weather. The GOES network also provides early detection and tracking of hurricanes.
